title: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head O (Ministry of Health)

sections.label: Middle-income family healthcare costs
sections.summary: A middle-income family still pays over $12,000 per year even with the latest subsidies, before transport, home care, medications and lost caregiver income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even with the latest subsidies, a middle-income family still pays over $12,000 per year, before transport, home care, medications, and lost caregiver income.

sections.label: Prevention share of healthcare budget
sections.summary: Singapore invests 6% of its healthcare Budget in population-level prevention, with plans to double it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore is investing in population-level prevention – 6 % of our healthcare Budget, with plans to double.

sections.label: Subsidised specialist consultation and scan
sections.summary: When referred by a Healthier SG GP, the first specialist consultation and primary CT or MRI scan should be subsidised, public or private.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When referred by a Healthier SG general practitioner (GP), the first specialist consultation and primary diagnostic scan, CT or MRI, public or private, should be subsidised.

sections.label: MediSave flex withdrawal limit proposal
sections.summary: Noting Singaporeans face long-term costs even with subsidies, the passage proposes MediSave flex with an annual withdrawal limit linked to balances and an upper cap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Even with subsidies, Singaporeans face costs over the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I propose MediSave flex where the annual withdrawal limit is linked to balances, with an upper cap to maintain sustainability.

sections.label: Study recalibrating S+3M
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will commit to studying and reporting, ideally before the next Budget, how S+3M can be recalibrated for chronic and preventive care.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry commit to studying and reporting, ideally before the next Budget, how S+3M can be recalibrated to better support chronic and preventive care?

sections.label: Chronic disease screening participation rate
sections.summary: Only about six in 10 eligible residents participate regularly in recommended chronic disease screenings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Yet today, only about six in 10 eligible residents participate regularly in recommended chronic disease screenings.

sections.label: Opt-out screenings and health coaching
sections.summary: The speaker proposes moving to opt-out screenings and proactive personalised health coaching supported by digital nudges, noting opt-in assumes time, awareness and confidence not everyone has.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Opt-in assumes time, awareness and confidence – luxuries not everyone has.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: I propose: move to opt-out screenings, proactive, personalised health coaching supported by digital nudges.

sections.label: Opt-out preventive programmes question
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will consider making key preventive programmes opt-out and how it will embed preventive defaults across Government.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider making key preventive programmes opt-out and outline how the Ministry will work across Government to embed preventive defaults in daily life?

sections.label: Singapore health data foundations
sections.summary: Singapore has laid strong foundations: HEALIX analytics, NEHR patient records, the Health Information Bill, and early AI pilots easing clinician workload and improving outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Singapore has laid strong foundations: HEALIX enables analytics across clusters; the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) aggregates patient records; the Health Information Bill clarifies rights, responsibilities and safeguards; and early AI pilots are already easing clinician workload and improving patient outcomes.

sections.label: Healthcare AI roadmap and MediSave limits
sections.summary: The question asks for a roadmap with timelines for data access, validation standards and talent, and notes MediSave and IP withdrawal limits have not risen for close to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Will the Ministry outline a clear roadmap, with timelines, for strengthening data access frameworks, validation standards and talent development, so Singapore leads in trusted healthcare AI?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The MediSave contribution ceiling in 2015 was $48,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, its equivalent – the Basic Healthcare Sum of the maximum amount in the MediSave account – is $79,000, an increase of about $30,000 in a period of about 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With close to 70% of locals holding an Integrated Shield Plan (IP), there has been no increase for close to 10 years since the introduction of MediShield Life with respect to the maximum amount one could use from MediSave to service IP premiums, or what is referred to as annual withdrawal limits.

sections.label: Healthcare workforce growth projection
sections.summary: The Ministry has shared that the healthcare workforce is projected to grow by 20% from 129,000 in 2024 to about 156,000 in 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry has shared that the healthcare workforce is projected to grow by 20% from 129,000 in 2024 to about 156,000 in 2030.

sections.label: Concern over policyholder conversion strain
sections.summary: There are deep concerns that 100,000 policyholders converting yearly from private to public healthcare coverage may significantly strain the public healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Second, there are deep concerns that the addition of 100,000 policyholders converting their insurance coverage from the private to public healthcare sector each year may significantly strain the public healthcare system.

sections.label: Surgery, chemotherapy and reconstruction coverage
sections.summary: She had surgery, complications, continued chemotherapy and reconstruction, but parts of her reconstruction were deemed cosmetic and not covered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: She faced surgery, complications of surgery and continued chemotherapy for her condition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: She underwent reconstruction, but parts of her reconstruction were not covered because it was deemed to be cosmetic.

sections.label: Hereditary risk assessment and financing prevention
sections.summary: She asks how hereditary risk assessment and genetic counselling can be integrated into primary care and Healthier SG, and whether financing of preventive procedures and reconstruction will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, how can we integrate hereditary risk assessment and genetic counselling into primary care and connect it to Healthier SG so that prevention becomes upstream?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, will the Ministry review how we finance medically indicated preventive procedures and the reconstruction, including high-risk situations involving a currently healthy organ, so that support is consistent and understandable?

sections.label: Precision medicine and functional health markers
sections.summary: She asks about the Ministry's pathway to evaluate precision and longevity-related medicine, and how Healthier SG can add metabolic, cognitive and frailty indicators.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: First, what is the Ministry's pathway to evaluate and adopt emerging evidence in precision and longevity-related medicine with clear safeguards for safety and value?

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Second, how can Healthier SG progressively add functional health markers, including metabolic, cognitive and frailty indicators, so that prevention becomes personalised and not just generic?

sections.label: Cancer Drug List and integrated plan riders
sections.summary: The Cancer Drug List has about 394 subsidised drugs, and from April new integrated plan riders cannot cover the minimum deductible, with co-payment capped at $6,000 yearly and premiums about 30% lower.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For instance, the Cancer Drug List now has about 394 drugs listed that are eligible for subsidies and claims under MediShield Life and integrated plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With effect from April this year, new riders on integrated plans can no longer cover the minimum deductible set by MOH while the co-payment of bills at 5% of the total bill will be capped at $6,000 per year instead of $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With these changes, the premiums for the new riders are expected to be about 30% lower than for the existing riders.

sections.label: Parents losing benefits when moving in
sections.summary: When children bring ageing parents into their homes, the parents often lose benefits such as CHAS, Silver Support or other subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: When children bring ageing parents into their homes, the parents often lose their benefits, such as the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS), Silver Support or other subsidies.

sections.label: Independent assessment for seniors moving in
sections.summary: Seniors moving into an adult child's home for caregiving should be assessed independently instead of being lumped into the entire household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Victor Lye (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Seniors moving into an adult child's home for caregiving should be assessed independently instead of being lumped into the entire household.

sections.label: MediSave balances and claim limits
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng reported MediSave balances exceed Retirement Accounts, and proposed carrying over unspent limits and age-tiered claim limits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In response to a Parliamentary Question posed in 2022, Minister Tan See Leng reported that MediSave account balances for members significantly exceed their Retirement Accounts, with the ratio for those aged 85 and above close to five times larger.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, we can permit carrying over of unspent limits for up to three years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, we can have a tiered system of claim limits, with the amounts allowed for claims gradually raised according to age.

sections.label: Flexible MediSave withdrawals for seniors
sections.summary: The Ministry should allow more flexible MediSave withdrawals at public healthcare institutions for patients over 60 with significant balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Ministry should allow for more flexible MediSave withdrawals at public healthcare institutions for patients over 60, especially for those with significant MediSave balances.

sections.label: Custodial care and step-down facilities
sections.summary: The question asks whether plans exist to develop more custodial care and step-down facilities so IMH beds are reserved for full clinical expertise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: My third question is whether there are plans to develop more custodial care and step-down facilities – sheltered homes, supported living – so that IMH’s beds are reserved for those who need its full clinical expertise?

sections.label: Cost of mental health conditions
sections.summary: Mental health conditions cost Singapore around $16 billion annually, largely from lost productivity due to absenteeism and presenteeism.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mental health conditions cost Singapore around $16 billion annually, largely from lost productivity due to absenteeism and presenteeism.

sections.label: Sustaining demand and national strategy
sections.summary: The question is whether the system can sustain demand ahead, and the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy was launched.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The question is whether our system is built to sustain the demand ahead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: We launched the National Mental Health and Well-being Strategy.

sections.label: Mental Health Office role and mandate
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to elaborate on the role and mandate of the Mental Health Office.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister elaborate on the role and mandate of the Mental Health Office?

sections.label: MOH projecting mental health manpower
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOH is projecting manpower needs for clinical psychologists and allied mental health professionals over the next five to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: How is MOH projecting manpower needs for clinical psychologists and allied mental health professionals over the next five to 10 years?

sections.label: AI role in mental healthcare
sections.summary: The passage asks how MOH views AI's role in mental healthcare, what safeguards are needed, and for an update and commitment to fixed timelines to regulate mental health professionals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share how MOH is thinking about the role of AI in mental healthcare and what safeguards may be needed to ensure that technology compliments, rather than replaces, trained professionals?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: With the mental health crisis showing no signs of abating, would the Ministry provide an update along with a firm commitment to fixed timelines to regulate mental health professionals?

sections.label: Mental health share of healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: The passage states MOH dedicated around 3% of healthcare expenditure to mental health between 2020 and 2022, and asks if this increased and projected amounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Between 2020 and 2022, MOH dedicated around 3% of its healthcare expenditure towards mental health treatment, promotion and prevention.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Has this amount increased, and what are the projected amounts going forward?

sections.label: Cohort smoking ban policies
sections.summary: The passage states Maldives' policy has come into effect and the UK Bill is set for implementation at the start of 2027, citing a Nottingham University study on a cohort ban.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Maldives' policy has already come into effect, while the United Kingdom (UK) Bill is on track to becoming law, is set to be implemented at the start of 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The latest studies, including a Nottingham University study published in January, suggest that a cohort ban will bring forward by decades a smoking prevalence of under 5%, which is defined as an effective endgame for tobacco.

sections.label: Atopic eczema and reporting framework
sections.summary: The passage states one in five children and one in 10 adults in Singapore have atopic eczema, and asks about adding it to the Chronic Disease Management Programme and a tiered reporting framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In Singapore, one in five children and one in 10 adults endure the constant, debilitating itch of this atopic eczema.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider adding atopic eczema to the Chronic Disease Management Programme, which already covers similar conditions like psoriasis?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: To encourage greater help-seeking while ensuring safety, will the Ministry implement a tiered reporting framework that allows for greater confidentiality in a risk-proportionate manner?

sections.label: Single coordination point for care
sections.summary: The passage states Minister Ong spoke about a single coordination point for care and 85 sub-regions coordinating across several services with One Care Plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Minister Ong has spoken about a single coordination point for care and 85 sub-regions, which will soon provide coordination across Regional Health System, Home Personal Care Plus, Singapore Counselling Centre, Drug Rehabilitation Centre and Active Ageing Centres with One Ring to Rule… excuse me, One Care Plan to coordinate them all.

sections.label: Audiology and podiatry courses
sections.summary: A request for the Ministry to consider degree or diploma courses in audiology and podiatry in tertiary institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Fourth, I ask the Ministry to consider introducing degree or diploma courses for audiology and podiatry in tertiary institutions, to increase the number of Singaporeans specialising in these areas and in turn, be better able to serve our seniors who require such specialised care.

sections.label: Value of informal caregiving
sections.summary: A Duke-NUS study estimated informal caregiving time for seniors aged 75 and above requiring human assistance at about $1.28 billion a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Duke-National University of Singapore study estimated the monetary value of informal caregiving time for seniors, aged 75 and above, who require human assistance, at about $1.28 billion a year.

sections.label: Long-term care financing and carer passport
sections.summary: Budget 2026 tops up the Long-term Care Support Fund by $400 million, and the Minister was asked to study a UK carer passport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Budget 2026 strengthens long-term care financing, including a $400 million top-up to the Long-term Care Support Fund to fund additional subsidies from CareShield Life enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But financing alone will not solve the recognition and navigation problem, so I asked the Minister to study and pilot a simple tool used in parts of the United Kingdom (UK) – a carer passport.

sections.label: Caregiver passport pilot proposal
sections.summary: The caregiver passport should involve caregivers in care planning and linkage, with two to three precinct pilots of about 100 caregivers each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More importantly, the caregiver passport should also allow caregivers to be involved in discharge and care planning, speed up linkage to respite and training, enable structured workplace flexibility conversations and support daily life participation through community partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose starting with two to three precinct pilots, for six to nine months, enrolling about 100 caregivers per pilot, followed by an evaluation to measure take up, navigation outcomes and changes to caregiver strain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, will MOH seed a caregiver recognition pilot fund to support these pilots, including evaluation, so we can scale up works?

sections.label: Triple wins programme aims
sections.summary: The programme aims for triple wins: children's academic success, older adults' well-being, and stronger communities through connecting generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: The programme aims for "triple wins": first, to help children succeed academically, especially in early literacy; two, boost the physical, mental and social well-being of older adults; and three, strengthen communities by connecting generations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Volunteers experience reduced depression, enhanced cognitive function and stronger social connections.

sections.label: Silver Guardian volunteering programme
sections.summary: MOH's Silver Guardian programme encourages seniors to volunteer at Active Ageing Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: MOH's Silver Guardian programme encourages seniors to volunteer at Active Ageing Centres.

sections.label: Singapore seniors pandemic mental health study
sections.summary: A peer-reviewed Singapore study of adults aged 21 to 89 found seniors reported significantly lower depression, anxiety and stress than younger adults during the 2020 pandemic lockdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: A peer-reviewed Singapore study of adults aged 21 to 89 found that seniors reported significantly lower levels of depression, anxiety and stress than younger adults during the 2020 pandemic lockdown.

sections.label: Speaker on behavioural addiction attention
sections.summary: The speaker rises to ask whether sufficient attention is paid to a possibly emerging behavioural addiction, particularly among young people, and public health's role.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Today, I rise not to moralise or to condemn desire.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: I rise to ask whether we are paying sufficient attention to a behavioural addiction that may be quietly emerging, particularly amongst our young people, and to consider what role public health can and should play.

sections.label: Community help for compulsive sexual behaviours
sections.summary: Community organisations observed rising help-seeking for compulsive sexual behaviours, with post-pandemic online pornography cases more than doubling and some teenagers as young as 12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Locally, community organisations, such as We Care Community Services, have observed an increase in the number of individuals seeking help for compulsive sexual behaviours, including problematic pornography use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Reporting cases relating to sex, porn and love addiction have risen significantly in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Post-pandemic, those seeking help for online pornography behaviours more than doubled compared with pre-COVID levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Some cases have also appeared among teenagers, with some of them as young as 12; 12, Sir!

sections.label: Youth arrests for sexual crimes 2024
sections.summary: In 2024, more than 460 youths aged 19 and below were arrested for sexual crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: In 2024, more than 460 youths aged 19 and below were arrested for sexual crimes.

sections.label: Call for national pornography study
sections.summary: Much understanding is extrapolated from international research and community case reports, and the speaker calls for a rigorous interdisciplinary national study on problematic pornography use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Much of our understanding is extrapolated from international research and community case reports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: First, commission a rigorous, interdisciplinary national study on problematic pornography use in Singapore.

sections.label: Review digital and sexuality education
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a review of Singapore's digital and sexuality education frameworks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Second, review our digital and sexuality education frameworks.

sections.label: Community addiction services funding
sections.summary: Funding and capacity for community addiction services are being expanded to keep pace with rising demand for behavioural addiction counselling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: Third, expanding funding and capacity for community addiction services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Queenstown)
sentences.text: If demand for counselling related to behavioural addictions is rising, our support ecosystem must keep pace.

sections.label: Singapore becoming super-aged society
sections.summary: Singapore is expected to become a super-aged society this year as citizens aged 65 and above reach 21%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Singapore is expected to become a super-aged society this year as the proportion of citizens aged 65 and above reaches 21%.

sections.label: Scaling up home care technology
sections.summary: A question asks if the Ministry can elaborate on plans to scale up technology deployment through Enhanced Home Personal Care and other programmes.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Terence Ho (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard I would like to ask if the Ministry could elaborate on plans to scale up technology deployment through the Enhanced Home Personal Care service and other programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: One in two who are healthy at 65 years old, are expected to develop severe disability at some point in their lifetime.

sections.label: Enhanced caregiver support since 2019
sections.summary: Launched in 2019, caregiver support has been enhanced in respite care, subsidy levels and the Home Caregiving Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Launched in 2019, caregiver support has been enhanced in a few areas, including respite care, subsidy levels and the Home Caregiving Grant.

sections.label: Expanding Home Caregiving Grant eligibility
sections.summary: A question asks whether the means-tested Home Caregiving Grant will be expanded to caregivers of family members needing one to two ADL.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Second, whether the Ministry will consider expanding the means-tested Home Caregiving Grant to provide more support for more caregivers, including those who care for family members who require assistance with one to two Activities of Daily Living (ADL), below the current eligibility of three ADL today.

sections.label: Dementia and osteoporosis rates above 70
sections.summary: Based on 2023 data, 11% of those above 70 have dementia and 16% have osteoporosis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: First, based on 2023 data, 11% of those above the age of 70 have dementia and 16% above the age of 70 have osteoporosis.

sections.label: Pre-dementia screening and bone density
sections.summary: Pre-dementia screening and Bone Density Tests allow early detection, timely intervention and better long-term planning, and the Ministry said Care Protocols for Dementia and Osteoporosis were being developed under Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Pre-dementia screening and Bone Density Tests allow for: one, early detection; two, timely intervention which can slow down the progression; and three, better long-term planning, which gives our seniors and their families the time and opportunity to make necessary adjustments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I had asked a Parliamentary Question in September 2025 on whether the Ministry had plans to include as part of the Healthier SG Programme, screenings for pre-dementia and osteoporosis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I was heartened when the Ministry had indicated that Care Protocols for Dementia and Osteoporosis were being developed under Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Second, according to the National Population Health Survey 2024 conducted by the Health Promotion Board, 54.7% of Singapore residents in the oldest age band, 60 to 74 years, were least willing to seek help from healthcare professionals, while 70.9% of those aged 30 to 39 were the most willing to do so.

sections.label: Healthier SG mental health protocols
sections.summary: In the Committee of Supply 2025 debates it was announced that Healthier SG care protocols for major depressive disorder and general anxiety disorder would be rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the Committee of Supply 2025 debates, it was announced at that Healthier SG care protocols for major depressive disorder and general anxiety disorder would be rolled out.

sections.label: Social prescribing referral options
sections.summary: Social prescribing is already part of the system under Healthier SG, but referral options remain narrow, largely involving Active Ageing Centres and Sports SG.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My three asks are about making them work together.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome that social prescribing is already part of our system under Healthier SG, but the referral options remain narrow, largely involving Active Ageing Centres and Sports SG, while the ecosystem around is wide.

sections.label: Minister on social determinants
sections.summary: The Minister said in Geneva in May 2023 that 60% of health is socially determined, in homes and communities, and the ask is to scale the Living Asset Map across all three clusters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Minister himself said in Geneva in May 2023, that 60% of health is socially determined, not in hospitals, but in homes and in communities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My first ask follows from his words: scale the Living Asset Map across all three clusters.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment figures
sections.summary: Healthier SG has enrolled over 1.3 million Singaporeans as of August 2025, but enrolment is not yet activation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Healthier SG has enrolled over 1.3 million Singaporeans as of August 2025, but enrolment is not yet activation.

sections.label: Publishing patient engagement data
sections.summary: The passage asks to publish how many enrolled patients stay and how many actively engaged through follow-ups, screenings and care team visits.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Publish how many enrolled patients stay and how many actively engaged through follow-ups, screenings and care team visits?

sections.label: AI-assisted imaging and remote monitoring
sections.summary: AI-assisted imaging, predictive analytics, earlier risk stratification and remote monitoring allow intervention before deterioration becomes crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: AI-assisted imaging, predictive analytics under Healthier SG, earlier risk stratification for cardiovascular disease and remote monitoring of chronic conditions allow us to intervene before deterioration becomes crisis.

sections.label: Rehabilitation sensor and robotic technologies
sections.summary: Sensor-guided therapy and robotic technologies, including exoskeleton-assisted gait training for selected patients, can safely increase therapy intensity in early recovery.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In rehabilitation, sensor-guided therapy systems and carefully deployed robotic technologies, including exoskeleton-assisted gait training for selected patients, can increase therapy intensity safely and consistently, particularly in early recovery.

sections.label: Embedding functional indicators alongside utilisation metrics
sections.summary: Scaling AI and rehabilitation technologies should continue embedding functional indicators alongside utilisation metrics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As we scale AI and rehabilitation technologies, we should continue embedding functional indicators – mobility, independence, caregiver burden, re-admission reduction and return-to-community participation – alongside utilisation metrics.

sections.label: Scaling sustainable healthcare technologies
sections.summary: Scaling technologies must improve independence, strengthen professional capability and remain financially sustainable in a super-aged society, extending mobility, confidence and participation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In healthcare, that discipline means scaling technologies that demonstrably improve independence, strengthen professional capability and remain financially sustainable in a super-aged society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: As Singaporeans live longer, our ambition must be clear – not merely to extend years of life, but to extend years of mobility, confidence and participation.

sections.label: Healthier SG frailty and functional health protocols
sections.summary: Healthier SG Care Protocols on frailty and functional health, such as osteoporosis and dementia, are progressing well and roll out in 2028.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Mr Alex Yeo and Dr Hamid Razak would be pleased to know that the development of Healthier SG Care Protocols related to frailty and functional health, such as for osteoporosis and dementia are progressing well and would be rolled out in 2028.

sections.label: Enhanced community health posts in Woodlands
sections.summary: NHG Health is progressively enhancing 11 CHPs across Woodlands Town, offering walk-in services including health advice, assessments and social prescriptions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: We agree with Dr Haresh Singaraju's view that it is important to connect patients to community resources, and we are enhancing accessibility of health services by bringing care directly into the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that NHG Health has been progressively enhancing 11 CHPs across Woodlands Town since the start of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: All residents, including non-seniors, can walk-in to these enhanced CHPs to access services such as: general health advice, basic health assessments and social prescriptions which include linking up residents with community programmes and resources, support for preventive health and disease management; including health coaching, medication review and chronic disease and frailty management programmes, and support for caregivers and post-discharge follow-ups for patients returning home from hospitals.

sections.label: Woodlands Hospital community care initiative
sections.summary: Woodlands Hospital will launch an initiative from end of this month providing specialist-supported care through enhanced CHPs and teleconsultation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: To address this, Woodlands Hospital will launch a new initiative starting end of this month to provide specialist-supported care for patients in the community through the enhanced CHPs in Woodlands and direct teleconsultation with individuals.

sections.label: Estimated specialist visit savings
sections.summary: NHG Health estimates this will save about 500 physical specialist outpatient clinic visits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: NHG Health estimates this will save about 500 physical specialist outpatient clinic visits.

sections.label: Exercise sessions and Healthy 365 app
sections.summary: From April 2026 more residents can join workout sessions in community locations, with HPB enhancing the Healthy 365 app from June 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: From April 2026 onwards, more residents will be able to join workout and exercise sessions in familiar, convenient and spacious locations including community halls, plazas and malls near their homes, such as 888 Plaza and Fu Chun Community Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: HPB will enhance the Healthy 365 mobile app with wayfinding and gamification features to connect residents to nearby opportunities to stay healthy and active in their everyday environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For example, residents may be prompted to complete a brisk walk along park connectors or trails within their neighbourhood and complete digital "check-ins" at designated points.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This feature will roll out progressively from June 2026.

sections.label: Declining prevalence rate
sections.summary: Prevalence has declined over the years to 8.4% in 2024 and about 5% in young adults aged 18 to 29.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Prevalence has declined over the years, to 8.4% in 2024 and even lower in young adults aged 18 to 29 years at about 5%.

sections.label: Woodlands mosques CHP partnership
sections.summary: An Nur Mosque and Yusof Ishak Mosque in Woodlands will partner with NHG Health to provide CHP services by September 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: For many in our community, the mosque is such a setting that provides this support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: I am therefore pleased to announce that the two mosques in Woodlands, An Nur Mosque and Yusof Ishak Mosque, will be partnering with NHG Health to provide CHP services by September 2026.

sections.label: Jom Check! health screening trial
sections.summary: Since May 2025 HPB has trialed Jom Check! with healthcare partners, organising 16 sessions islandwide reaching more than 300 residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: By bringing healthcare services to familiar settings frequented by our community, and partnering with religious and community leaders, healthcare will become more accessible to our community To further encourage health screening among our Malay/Muslim community, since May 2025, the HPB has trialed the Jom Check!

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: This is done in collaboration with many healthcare partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: So far, 16 sessions have been organised islandwide, reaching more than 300 residents.

sections.label: Healthier SG enrolment rate
sections.summary: About 57% of eligible residents have enrolled into Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Today, about 57% of eligible residents have enrolled into Healthier SG.

sections.label: Obesity rate in community
sections.summary: Thirty-two percent, about one in three people, is obese, a rise of nearly 10 percentage points from 24% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Thirty-two percent, or about one in three people in our community, is obese, a rise of nearly 10 percentage points from 24% in 2020.

sections.label: Focus Area Five participation
sections.summary: Through Focus Area Five, more than 90,000 people participated in various programmes in 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
sentences.text: Through the efforts of Focus Area Five (FA5), more than 90,000 people have participated in various programmes in 2025.

sections.label: Singapore super-aged society
sections.summary: Singapore has crossed 21% and is now a super-aged society.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, we should have crossed 21% by now.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, as I speak, Singapore is a super-aged society.

sections.label: Early actions on demographic transition
sections.summary: Early actions include raising GST, retirement and re-employment ages, age-friendly streets and apartments, and financial security measures.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More importantly, we foresaw this demographic transition years ago and took as many early actions as we can.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This includes raising the Goods and Services Tax to strengthen our fiscal position; increasing the retirement and re-employment ages; building many more age-friendly streets and 2-room Flexi and senior apartments; and bolstering financial security for seniors through Silver Support, Central Provident Fund (CPF) LIFE and MediShield Life.

sections.label: Target for more hospital beds
sections.summary: The MOH Addendum set a target of adding 2,800 more public acute and community hospital beds between 2025 and 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the Opening of this term of Parliament, the MOH Addendum set out the target of adding 2,800 more public acute and community hospital beds between 2025 and 2030.

sections.label: Who pays national healthcare
sections.summary: National healthcare expenditure is ultimately paid by the people through charges, taxes, insurance premiums and medical security contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: National healthcare expenditure – that is the hospital bill of the nation.

sentences.speaker: The Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: That bill, remember this, is always and ultimately paid by the people, whether through healthcare charges, through taxes, through insurance premiums, through medical security contributions.

sections.label: Healthcare spending in developed economies
sections.summary: Developed economies typically spend around 9% to 12% of GDP on healthcare, while the US spends 17%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Developed economies, shown by the different dots on screen, typically spend around 9% to 12% of gross domestic product (GDP) on healthcare, with the United States (US) – outlier in the other direction – spending 17%.

sections.label: Government health budget rise
sections.summary: The Government health budget is about 2.7% of GDP this year and is expected to rise to about 3.5% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Government health budget today is about 2.7% of GDP this year, and it is expected to rise to about 3.5% of GDP by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This 0.8 percentage point increase is actually very significant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It means increasing the Government's health budget from about $22.5 billion this year to about $30 billion in 2030.

sections.label: Budget share for aged care
sections.summary: The budget is 1.5 times that of 2021, with acute hospital care's share falling and aged care funding rising from 11% to 13%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The budget is 1.5 times that of 2021, but the share of acute hospital care has fallen, from three-quarters to almost two-thirds – the remaining one-third going to aged care and population health.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Specifically, the share of funding for aged care rose from 11% to 13% – that is the green portion – between 2021 and 2024.

sections.label: Shortening clinical psychologist training
sections.summary: Training time for clinical psychologists will be reduced from seven to eight years to about five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It is a key agenda, including how we will significantly shorten the time to train clinical psychologists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are taking seven to eight years currently; we will reduce it to about five years.

sections.label: AI chronic disease risk tool
sections.summary: An AI tool identifying high risk of chronic diseases within three years will be rolled out to doctors for Healthier SG enrolees from early 2027.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With this model, by reviewing an individual's current health status, it can identify if he/she has a high risk – high risk defined by 75% or above – of developing chronic diseases, such as diabetes or high cholesterol, within the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Many of these cases can be prevented if early actions were taken, such as through lifestyle adjustments and medication.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This AI risk assessment tool will be rolled out to doctors for all Healthier SG enrolees from early 2027.

sections.label: Subsidised genetic testing for HBOC
sections.summary: From December, subsidised genetic testing will be offered to at-risk individuals for HBOC, and to immediate family members if they test positive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From December this year, we will offer subsidised genetic testing to at risk individuals for HBOC, such as individuals with a family history of HBOC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And if they test positive, we will also offer the test to their immediate family members – cascade testing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We expect over 2,000 individuals to be eligible for the test annually.

sections.label: Coverage for HBOC preventive surgeries
sections.summary: MediShield Life and MediSave will be extended later this year to cover preventive surgeries for HBOC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Risk-reducing mastectomies for breast cancer prevention, and the removal of both fallopian tubes and ovaries for ovarian cancer prevention, fall within these criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will therefore extend MediShield Life and MediSave to cover preventive surgeries for HBOC later this year.

sections.label: Out-of-pocket costs after subsidies
sections.summary: After subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave, nine in 10 Singaporeans pay less than $500 out-of-pocket for subsidised in-patient bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With this design, after subsidies, MediShield Life and MediSave, nine in 10 Singaporeans pay less than $500 out-of-pocket for their subsidised in-patient bills.

sections.label: Changes to MediSave500/700 scheme
sections.summary: After increasing the Flexi-MediSave limit for seniors and doubling the annual limit for diagnostic scans, further changes will be made to the MediSave500/700 scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For example, we recently increased the Flexi-MediSave limit for seniors, and we doubled the annual limit for diagnostic scans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This time, we will make further changes to the MediSave500/700 scheme.

sections.label: Raising MediSave limits and CDMP conditions
sections.summary: MediSave limits will rise from $500/$700 to $700/$1,000, and the CDMP list will include hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Today, individuals with a simple chronic condition can use up to $500 a year, while those with complex chronic conditions can withdraw up to $700 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: To provide more support for preventive and chronic care in the community, we will raise MediSave limits from $500/$700 to $700/$1,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This will benefit over 910,000 patients who currently tap on the scheme, roughly 20% of whom have annual bills exceeding the withdrawal limits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will also expand the list of conditions covered under the CDMP to include hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism.

sections.label: Raising annual MediSave withdrawal limits
sections.summary: To make chronic disease medical expenses more affordable, the annual MediSave withdrawal limit will rise from $500 to $700 next year, and from $700 to $1,000 for complex conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, to make medical expenses for chronic diseases more affordable, we will raise the annual MediSave withdrawal limit from $500 to $700 starting next year, whilst the annual limit for chronic disease patients with more complex conditions will be raised from $700 to $1,000.

sections.label: Robotic surgery cost caution
sections.summary: Singapore is cautious about promoting robotic surgery, weighing cost effectiveness and patient affordability, and will adopt long-term policies with quality teams and cost-effective technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For example, in the Chinese hospitals I visited, some traditional surgeries have already been replaced by robotic surgery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: However, robotic surgery is very costly, and these expenses are often borne by the patients themselves, causing medical insurance premiums to increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Therefore, in Singapore, we are very cautious when promoting robotic surgery or any other technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We must consider both cost effectiveness and patient affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: From Hippocrates to Hua Tuo (華佗), to AI and robotic surgery, the medical field has been advancing rapidly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We will take a multi-pronged approach to adopt long-term policies and make use of high-quality medical teams and cost-effective technology to bring better medical services to our people. : Mr Chairman, when I informed the House three years ago that we would be a super-aged society this year, it was not to instil fear, but to prepare ourselves.

sections.label: Healthier longer lives
sections.summary: What matters is that Singaporeans are not just living longer but living healthier for longer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What matters is that Singaporeans are not just living for longer; we are living healthier for longer.

sections.label: Hospital Clinician as PD
sections.summary: Under the new care team model, a trained and assessed competent Hospital Clinician may take on the PD role to supervise, oversee and coordinate care.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Under the new care team model, a PD need not be a specialist.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Once they are trained and assessed to be competent, a Hospital Clinician may take on the role of a PD to supervise, oversee and coordinate care, incorporating the inputs of various healthcare professionals.

sections.label: Heartland dental care subsidies
sections.summary: CHAS dental subsidies were enhanced and polyclinic dental services expanded with community dental partners to bring affordable dental care closer to seniors' homes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In response to Mr Cai Yinzhou's query on the provision of specialist dental, audiology and podiatry services in the heartlands, we recently enhanced Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) subsidies for dental care and are expanding dental services at polyclinics and strengthening partnerships with community dental providers – moves that will bring affordable dental care closer to where our seniors live.

sections.label: Podiatry and foot screening
sections.summary: Podiatry services are at selected polyclinics, while foot screening for diabetes patients is at all polyclinics and Healthier SG GPs through Primary Care Networks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Additionally, while podiatry services are available at selected polyclinics, foot screening services for patients with diabetes are available at all polyclinics as well as Healthier SG GPs through their respective Primary Care Networks.

sections.label: Healthcare expenditure share of GDP
sections.summary: National healthcare expenditure is 4.4% of GDP, less than half of what other countries spent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: On the other hand, our national healthcare expenditure is at 4.4% of our GDP, which is less than half of what other countries spent.

sections.label: Hospitals tapping extra facilities
sections.summary: Hospitals can tap facilities like Transitional Care Facilities and Mobile Inpatient Care @ Home to augment overall capacity if required.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: If required, hospitals can also tap on facilities, like the Transitional Care Facilities and the Mobile Inpatient Care @ Home, to augment overall capacity.

sections.label: IMH national psychiatric services centre
sections.summary: IMH will continue as national centre for psychiatric services, focusing on quaternary care for patients with more complex mental health needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: With the increased demand in mental health services, the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) will continue to serve as national centre for psychiatric services and focus on providing quaternary care to patients with more complex mental health needs.

sections.label: Growing healthcare workforce by 2030
sections.summary: The current healthcare workforce is broadly adequate, but must grow by 20% by 2030 to meet projected manpower demand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Our current healthcare workforce is broadly adequate for the population's healthcare demand.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will need to grow our healthcare workforce by 20% by 2030 to meet the projected manpower demand.

sections.label: Accelerated pathway for clinical psychologists
sections.summary: With MOE and NUS, eligible undergraduates get an accelerated pathway to specialise in Clinical Psychology at Master's level, first intake 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: To Dr Wan Rizal's query on strengthening the local pipeline of clinical psychologists while maintaining professional standards, we have worked with the Ministry of Education and NUS to offer eligible undergraduate students an accelerated pathway to specialise in Clinical Psychology at Master's level, with the first intake in 2026.

sections.label: Salary increases for healthcare staff
sections.summary: In 2025, salaries of allied health professionals, pharmacists and administrative, ancillary and support staff in public healthcare institutions rose by up to 7%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: In 2025, we have also increased the salaries of allied health professionals (AHPs), pharmacists and administrative, ancillary and support staff in public healthcare institutions by up to 7%.

sections.label: Shared competencies in allied health training
sections.summary: With IHLs, shared competencies are being built across allied health training programmes, rolled out progressively from Academic Year 2027 students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: For AHPs, we are working with IHLs to build up shared competencies across relevant allied health training programmes to better support a team-based shared-care model.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: These will be rolled out progressively, starting with students who begin their studies from Academic Year 2027 onwards.

sections.label: Registering higher risk psychologists
sections.summary: Five higher risk sub-disciplines of psychologists will be registered to ensure high standards of practice, ethics and professional conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Ms He Ting Ru has asked for an update on the regulation of mental health professionals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: We will be registering five higher risk sub-disciplines of psychologists to ensure high standards of practice, ethics and professional conduct so that our people receive safer and higher quality psychological services.

sections.label: Registration schedule announcement timeline
sections.summary: The detailed registration schedule, requirements and roadmaps will be announced by early 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The detailed registration schedule, requirements and roadmaps will be announced by early 2027.

sections.label: Expanding CREST and COMIT
sections.summary: By 2030, the number of CREST and COMIT will be expanded to 75 and 35 respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: By 2030, we will expand the number of CREST and COMIT to 75 and 35 respectively.

sections.label: Training frontline personnel and volunteers
sections.summary: Over 160,000 frontline personnel and volunteers were trained under the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework to identify and guide individuals in mental distress.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Fourth, we are enhancing capabilities of community service providers through the National Mental Health Competency Training Framework and have trained over 160,000 frontline personnel and volunteers to identify and guide individuals in mental distress to support avenues.

sections.label: No wrong door approach
sections.summary: A "no wrong door" approach facilitates access to services and right-siting care in primary and community settings, encouraging early help-seeking while avoiding over-medicalising mental health needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Adopting a "no wrong door" approach to facilitate access to services and right-siting care in primary and community settings encourage individuals to seek help early in non-stigmatising environments while avoiding over-medicalising mental health needs.

sections.label: National Addiction Management Service and ageing
sections.summary: The National Addiction Management Service provides treatment and assistance for addictions, and by 2030 one in four Singaporeans will be 65 and older.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The National Addiction Management Service, situated within the IMH, was established to provide treatment and assistance for individuals seeking help for addictions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The National Addiction Management Service specialises in addiction medicine research, which includes intoxicating substance use and emerging areas of concern such as Internet and gaming.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: MOH, together with the Ministry of Social and Family Development, and National Council of Social Service, and other stakeholders across sectors, will continue to develop and enhance access to addictions services in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As we navigate the road ahead and future challenges together, these three pillars will work in tandem to strengthen the core foundation of our healthcare system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: By 2030, one in four Singaporeans will be 65 years and older, and one in four of them will be aged 80 and above.

sections.label: Chronic disease among seniors
sections.summary: If half of seniors have at least one chronic disease, close to half a million will need care in 2030, up from about 400,000 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: If half of our seniors have at least one chronic disease, we will have to care for close to half a million of them in 2030, up from about 400,000 of them last year.

sections.label: SGO preventive health visits
sections.summary: Since 2022, SGO has started preventive health visits, engaged over 600,000 seniors and connected those with needs to services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Since 2022, SGO has started preventive health visits, engaged more than 600,000 seniors and connected those with needs to services like AACs, Senior Care Centres (SCCs) and community mental health services.

sections.label: LifeSG app and AAC network
sections.summary: Seniors who have not used the service can check the LifeSG app, and the AAC network grew from 154 to over 230 centres, serving around 100,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: For seniors who have not yet availed themselves to this service, please check out the LifeSG app.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We have also grown the AAC network from 154 centres to over 230 over the last two years, now serving around 100,000 seniors.

sections.label: Enhanced Home Personal Care service
sections.summary: From 1 April, more than 5,600 eligible seniors and caregivers can benefit from enhanced Home Personal Care with respite care, medication reminders and monitoring.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: From 1 April, more than 5,600 eligible seniors and their caregivers can benefit from the enhanced Home Personal Care service, featuring home-based respite care, medication reminders and 24/7 technology-enabled monitoring for fall detection and incident reporting.

sections.label: Seniors needing daily activity help
sections.summary: By 2030, around 100,000 seniors will need help with at least one daily activity like eating or showering.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: By 2030, around 100,000 seniors will need help with at least one daily activity like eating or showering.

sections.label: Single assessment for long-term care
sections.summary: From next month, seniors requiring multiple long-term care services will need only one comprehensive assessment by Integrated Community Care Providers using a standardised tool.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: From next month, seniors requiring multiple long-term care services will need only one comprehensive assessment done by the Integrated Community Care Providers using a standardised, internationally-recognised tool.

sections.label: NEHR Connect Grant launch
sections.summary: The National Electronic Health Record Connect Grant will be launched and opened for application in July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Third, we will launch the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) Connect Grant and open it for application in July this year.

sections.label: MOH funding for grant
sections.summary: MOH will set aside up to $45 million for this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: MOH will set aside up to $45 million for this.

sections.label: GPs viewing patient records
sections.summary: From July this year, GPs can view patients' health records documented by specialists, hospitals and other medical institutions in their computer systems.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: From July this year, GPs can view patients' health records previously documented by specialists, hospitals and other medical institutions in their computer systems.

sections.label: Connected health system for seniors
sections.summary: Services will expand so every senior can receive care and support, supported by the Health Information Act and digital health priorities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We will also continue to expand these services, so that every senior can receive the care and support they need.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We want our treasures – our seniors at home – to live happily and age well at home. : Through the Health Information Act and other digital health priorities, we are building a more connected, responsive and secure health system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This is in support of our broader healthcare transformation to anchor care in the community with more coordinated services that wrap around our seniors.

sections.label: MediSave use for chronic care
sections.summary: The Minister was asked how much MediSave is used for chronic and preventive care and whether modelling was done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Minister shared data on the healthcare expenditure on preventive care, for example, but how much of MediSave is used today for chronic and preventive care?

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And has the Ministry done any modelling on if we made MediSave chronic, MediSave preventive care, based on balances, how would that actually impact the sustainability?

sections.label: Distribution of balances
sections.summary: Two in 10 have less than $1,000, five in 10 have $1,000 to $10,000, and three in 10 have more than $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Two in 10 have less than $1,000; five in 10 have $1,000 to $10,000; three in 10 have more than $10,000.

sections.label: Halal and healthy food choices
sections.summary: The Ministry will sit together and work with other agencies, including the National Environment Agency, on halal and healthy food choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On more halal food choices, healthy choices, let us sit together and see whether we can work together with other agencies, including the National Environment Agency.

sections.label: Trust in care providers
sections.summary: The question asks how the Ministry will help the national effort to get patients and citizens to understand and trust care providers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Haresh Singaraju (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How exactly will the Ministry help in terms of the national effort to get patients and citizens to understand and trust the care that these providers provide?

sections.label: Osteoporosis and hereditary cancer coverage
sections.summary: The Member welcomes care protocols for osteoporosis such as frailty from 2028 and hereditary cancers being included as part of coverage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Chairman, I would like to ask two clarifications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: I really welcome the care protocols for osteoporosis, such as frailty, from 2028.

sentences.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Really, I think a lot of the physicians will welcome that hereditary cancers will now be included as part of the coverage.

sections.label: HBOC and MediShield Life modelling
sections.summary: Modelling was done because risk-reducing mastectomy saves future treatment costs, and the impact on MediShield Life is negligible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On HBOC, I hope I get the Member's question right.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We actually did the modelling because risk-reducing mastectomy saves future treatment costs and overall, actually, the impact on MediShield Life is quite negligible, which is why we are prepared to do this.

sections.label: One doctor, one GP
sections.summary: The Member urges sticking to one doctor, one GP as family doctor, and asks new towns like Tengah to enrol as many people as possible for Healthier SG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We got to stick to one doctor, one GP, where he becomes our family doctor, advises us on the health of our family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, a new town, like Tengah, please go for it and get as many people as we can, enrol for Healthier SG.

sections.label: Health programmes in Tengah town
sections.summary: The Ministry is happy to work with Dr Choo and other agencies to see what other health programmes can be implemented in Tengah town.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Beyond that, we will be more than happy to work with Dr Choo, with other agencies, to see what other health programmes we can implement in the Tengah town.

sections.label: Initial intake phase numbers
sections.summary: The initial phase of intake will only be about 10.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The course, I think the initial phase of intake will only be about for 10.

sections.label: Psychologist numbers and registration
sections.summary: There is no accurate count of psychologists, but the Singapore Psychological Society has about 1,700 members, mostly practising clinically, taken as a ballpark for registration.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, we do not really have an accurate number how many psychologists there are out there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But offhand, the Singapore Psychological Society has about 1,700 members.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Most of them are also practising in the clinical space.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, if we take that as a ballpark, that is roughly probably the numbers that we are going to start with when we formally do the registration.

sections.label: Entry criteria and course subsidies
sections.summary: They must minimally meet entry criteria, which cannot be lowered, while other support like course fee subsidies will largely align with what IHLs have today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But I would say, minimally, they will have to meet entry criteria, because that standard is not something we can lower.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But beyond that, other support measures, like whether there will be subsidies for the course fees, it will largely, my understanding is, it will be in line with what the IHLs have today.

sections.label: Annual review and MediSave focus
sections.summary: The review happens every year, the wish list will be reviewed entirely next time, and MediSave's focus is acknowledged amid tension between lumpy episodes and recurrent expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We review this every year and the next time, we will review the wish list entirely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: But to manage the Member's expectation a little bit, the focus of MediSave, I totally get the tension between big lumpy episodes versus recurrent expenses.

sections.label: Medium-term Healthier SG impact
sections.summary: Medium-term, they hope to make some impact on enrolment into Healthier SG, follow-up with check-ups, screening rate and vaccination rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Medium-term, we are hoping to make some impact in terms of enrolment into Healthier SG, follow up with the check-ups, rate of screening, rate of vaccinations.

sections.label: Audiologist certification standards
sections.summary: A qualified audiologist in Singapore needs higher certification as a diploma may not suffice, and while an in-between may be sought, standards cannot be sacrificed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In general, a qualified audiologist in Singapore needs a higher level of certification because a diploma level may not be quite enough to perform the task.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, we will look and see whether there is a way to actually find an in-between.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But ultimately, we cannot sacrifice standards just to meet the needs of people who want to take a shorter course to get there.

sections.label: Tracking one's own life
sections.summary: The passage states that tracking realistically cannot be done because it is your life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Realistically, it cannot be tracked, because it is your life.

sections.label: Social prescriptions in Healthier SG
sections.summary: Social prescriptions are part of the One Care Assessment Plan under Healthier SG, where the care plan includes the social prescription.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: One of the questions was, whether social prescriptions are part of the One Care Assessment Plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: That is actually part of the Healthier SG, where the care plan also includes the social prescription.

sections.label: Integrated Community Care Provider rollout
sections.summary: The Integrated Community Care Provider framework is starting to roll out this year and over coming years across 84 sub-regions in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Mr Cai also asked if the the Integrated Community Care Provider and Agency for Integrated Care could cater for different sorts of activities, like faith-based volunteering or maybe for seniors who are interested in gardening as a social activity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I would say that we are just starting to roll out the the Integrated Community Care Provider framework starting this year and over the coming years, and this is a non-trivial exercise across 84 sub-regions in Singapore – bringing together different parties and partners.

sections.label: UK ground-up caregiver initiative
sections.summary: The information came from online resources about a UK ground-up initiative where parties from hospitals to supermarkets show care for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I must caveat to say that the information I got was what I could glean from online resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It is a ground-up initiative in the UK and it is a way for the different parties involved ranging from hospitals to supermarkets he mentioned supermarkets earlier – to show care and support for caregivers.

sections.label: KPIs for mental health services
sections.summary: The passage asks what KPIs the Senior Minister of State Koh could share, such as wait times, care continuity and crisis presentations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: What would the Senior Minister of State Koh be able to share what are their KPIs, for example, whether there is a reduction in average wait times, improve care continuity, reduce crisis presentations?

sections.label: Psychologist retention and First Stops
sections.summary: The passage asks about psychologist retention levels and states that First Stops for Mental Health, like mindline.sg, remove barriers to first contact.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Are there any retention levels for psychologists specifically?

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For example, specialist track, progression and the public sector pay competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But what is important is that putting forth the First Stops for Mental Health, which is accessible – for example, mindline.sg is 24 hours and is accessible and it is anonymous – would really remove the key barriers that are holding everyone back from seeking at least the first contact point to get some advice and seek further help.

sections.label: Online counselling suicide risk protocol
sections.summary: Counsellors who assess suicide risk try to convince the person to seek care, with a protocol to fast track them to a psychiatrist or IMH A&E.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, for example, if they receive counselling online or through a phone call and the counsellor assesses that this individual is at risk of suicide ideation, they will try their very best to convince the individual to step forward and receive care.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And if the person is prepared to come forth, there will be a protocol to fast track them to make sure that they receive immediate attention from a qualified psychiatrist or even present at the A&E in IMH, where care can be immediately rendered.

sections.label: Registration for higher risk psychologists
sections.summary: Registration gives formal recognition to those practising in higher risk sub-sectors in psychology and ensures quality, standards and support.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think let us take one step at a time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We are starting with registration to give formal recognition to those who are practising in higher risk sub-sectors in psychology and making sure that the quality, the standards and the support is given to them to deliver the care that the clients and the patients need.

sections.label: Carry over of unused annual limits
